main_text.l: Euclides lib. 1. defin. 15, Circulus, inquit, est
figura plana & rotunda æqualiter distans à medio siue
centro à quo centro omnes lineæ
pūcto α tā versus β δ quam versus
γ. ε æqualiter distat à pūcto
α ita vt si millena millia linearū
ducas ex α ad istam lineā ro-
tundam, omnes istæ lineæ futuræ sint inter se æquales.a,
(a. Circulum breuissime sic definitur : Κύκλος ἐστι χῶρος ἐπίπεδος ὑπὸ μιᾶς γραμμῆς περιεχόμενος.)
Theoremata Geometrica de Circulo sunt hæc;
nobilissima, vtpote per quam omnes reliquæ lineæ
Quod in quoque rerum genere est
perfectissimum, idem quoque in eodem genere est primum, nam
omnia imperfecta pendēt à perfectissimo, à quo autem
omnia pendent, id necessario est primum. Quod autem
demonstrat Aristoteles 8. Phys. cap. 9. & 2. de cœlo, cap. 4. nempe
nam si quis obiiciat, cum ducis

page.notes: Two diagrams: a circle with Greek letters β, γ, δ, ε, ζ, η, ϑ, ι and centre α, and a circle with letters α, β, γ. The word "ducis" stands below the second diagram, apparently a catchword-like line in the text block; it is printed as the last line of the page's text and has been kept. Greek in the foot note transcribed from a small, partly illegible print; the Greek may contain errors.
